title: Deferred slot reclaimer and persistent burst window
author: Nora Alvarez
description:
Summary:
Introduce a deferred slot reclaimer and a small persistent burst window to improve dedicated fleet stability during short spikes and busy-to-idle transitions. This PR implements a lightweight ledger that defers slot reclamation for a short decay period and a per-tenant persistent burst window that can be charged and slowly drained. The combined behavior reduces oscillation from aggressive decommits while preserving short-lived burst capacity for latency-sensitive requests.

Motivation and context:
We observed repeated churn on Dedicated pools when transient load spikes triggered immediate slot decommits; on scale-down the system reclaimed slots aggressively, which caused request latency regressions and frequent warmup churn. Existing borrow/burst mechanisms either sacrificed predictability or required long prewarming. This change targets short bursts (seconds-to-minutes) and is intended to complement the warm-pool prewarming strategies without replacing them.

What this PR does (high level):
- Add a DeferredSlotLedger component that records recent decommit intents and applies a short decay window (configurable per-pool) before actual slot reclamation. During the decay window a slot is marked as reclaim-pending and is eligible for reuse for instantaneous burst requests.
- Introduce PersistentBurstWindow per-tenant: a very small burst credit (default 3 concurrent slots or configurable) that persists across short idle periods and drains with a configurable half-life. Credits are replenished on steady allocation and on explicit burst buys.
- Update the ScaleDown reconciler to consult the DeferredSlotLedger before issuing platform deprovision calls; add a fast-path to cancel pending decommits when ephemeral load returns.
- Publish new telemetry: deferred_reclaims{pool,reason}, persistent_burst_credit_level{tenant,pool}, burst_credit_drained_events, and ledger_hit_ratio. Add unit and integration tests for the ledger and drain semantics.

Backward compatibility and rollout:
- Feature guarded behind a cluster feature-flag (defaults to off). Config knobs exposed in DedicatedPoolSpec for early dogfooding.
- No breaking API changes to customer-facing endpoints. Config additions are additive.

Checklist:
- [x] DeferredSlotLedger implementation and unit tests
- [x] PersistentBurstWindow with decay logic and tests
- [x] ScaleDown reconciler integration + e2e simulation test
- [x] Telemetry metrics and dashboards snippets
- [x] Docs: console config reference and operator migration note

Related work:
- Linear: ENG-2149 (reduce scale churn during transient spikes), ENG-2212 (burstable tenant accounting)
- Builds on prior warm-pool work but intentionally lighter weight than prewarm reservoir designs.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- We intentionally chose a short decay period (configurable default 90s) to avoid long-lived wasted capacity; this trades off some worst-case cost for improved latency and reduced churn.
- Persistent burst credit is intentionally small to avoid gaming the system and to ensure that long sustained load still triggers normal autoscaling.
- The ledger is kept in-memory per-pool with a small persisted checkpoint to survive controller restart; this keeps runtime fast but means very short outages may lose some pending reclaims (acceptable).

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests: ledger boundaries, concurrency, race conditions between reclaim and reuse.
- Integration: simulated scale-up/scale-down traces (uses the existing perf-sim harness).
- Added a small flakiness guard to one timing-sensitive test (increased timeouts) to reduce CI noise.

Merge notes:
- Squash-merge to keep history tidy.
- Follow-up: add a canary rollout (10% of pools) and a job that synthesizes spotty traffic to validate.

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/allocator/deferred_ledger.go — new ledger + tests
- pkg/allocator/persistent_burst.go — new credit logic + tests
- pkg/controller/scaledown_controller.go — consult ledger before doDecommit
- pkg/controller/metrics.go — new telemetry emission points
- deploy/helm/values.dedicated.yaml — feature flag + knobs

release_notes: Introduce a Deferred Slot Ledger and a small Persistent Burst Window to reduce Dedicated pool churn and improve latency during short spikes. Feature disabled by default behind a feature flag; configurable per-pool.
comments: Ben Gupta: Left some nits on naming and suggested a smaller default decay (60s) — I agree with the conservative default for initial rollout.
Nora Alvarez: Responded — added a Helm knob and note in docs; kept default at 90s after discussion to avoid premature reclaims in high-latency regions.
Sofia Li: Approved after verifying metrics and tests; requested a follow-up to add an alert for ledger_hit_ratio drop.
Ethan Martinez: Ran perf-sim locally; observed 18% reduction in scale churn in the short-burst scenario (attached simulation logs).
